# KYDE

> KYDE is the behavioral firewall for enterprise AI agents — cryptographic agent identity, real-time behavioral scope enforcement, tamper-evident audit trails, and out-of-policy blocking. Deployed via a single environment variable. No agent code changes required. Any LLM provider.

## Product

**Kyde Gateway** is a model-agnostic governance proxy that sits between AI agents and every LLM provider. It intercepts every inference call, verifies agent identity, enforces behavioral scope, blocks out-of-policy actions before they execute, and signs every entry into a hash-chained audit ledger.

Two tiers:
- **Kyde Gateway Sandbox** (free) — Observe layer: signed ledger, compliance dashboard, post-hoc DLP alerts. Audit and traction entry point.
- **Kyde Gateway Enterprise** (paid, €8–25K/month) — Govern layer: real-time blocking, agent identity enforcement, MCP per-tool policy, RBAC, SLA, managed signing infrastructure.

Every audit entry captures: who acted (cryptographic agent identity + role), what happened (prompt, tool calls, response), why it decided (causal context: full retrieval and reasoning chain), when (millisecond-precise timestamp), and cryptographic proof (Ed25519 signature + SHA-256 hash chain).

## Core problem KYDE solves

Enterprises deploying AI agents face four unanswered questions:
1. **Who acted?** — Agents share service accounts with no traceable identity or role boundaries.
2. **Why did it decide that?** — No causal context captured. Decisions cannot be reconstructed for human oversight or regulatory review.
3. **What are the boundaries?** — No behavioral scope enforcement. Agents can exceed their mandate without detection.
4. **What happened?** — Vendor-provided logs are software-only, mutable, and controlled by the provider — not an independent audit trail.

The structural reason governance fails when built inside agents: capable agents can bypass their own rules. KYDE sits outside the agent, in the data path, and cannot be overridden by agent logic.

## Three guarantees

**CONTROL** — Real-time enforcement, not post-hoc detection.
- Cryptographic agent identity per agent and role
- Behavioral scope enforcement: blocks out-of-policy actions before execution
- API allowlists, DLP prevention, MCP per-tool policy, circuit breakers per role
- Agent blocking and RBAC
- Human-in-the-loop alerts on policy violations

**TRACE** — Every action attributed, every decision reconstructable.
- Every action traced to a specific cryptographic agent identity
- Causal context capture: full retrieval context, tool calls, intermediate reasoning, response — as a single record per inference event
- Full decision chain reconstruction for human oversight (EU AI Act Article 14)
- Behavioral anomaly detection

**TRUTH** — Cryptographic audit trail. Court-ready. Regulator-ready.
- Ed25519-signed, SHA-256 hash-chained append-only ledger
- Tamper-evident: alter any entry, every subsequent link breaks
- Architecturally independent of LLM provider infrastructure
- Compliance PDF exports
- Designed for EU AI Act Articles 12, 14, 26 — DORA Article 30 — GDPR Article 35

## Deployment

Three modes, all requiring zero code changes to agent logic:
- **Environment variable**: `export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://gateway.kyde.com/v1`
- **Group Policy (GPO)**: enterprise fleet deployment, no developer action required
- **Hosted proxy**: managed SaaS, EU data residency

Target latency overhead: under 100ms. Provider coverage: all major LLM providers.

## Provider compatibility

OpenAI (GPT-4o, o1, o3), Anthropic (Claude Sonnet, Opus, Haiku), Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, Mistral, DeepSeek, Ollama, local models via LMStudio/vLLM, MCP routing.

## Regulatory context

**EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689)**
High-Risk AI system enforcement deadline for Annex III (employment, credit, insurance, education, critical infrastructure, essential services): **December 2, 2027** (Digital Omnibus agreement, May 2026). Annex I embedded AI products: August 2028.

Key obligations for enterprises deploying AI agents:
- Article 12: Automatic logging throughout system lifecycle, tamper-evident, minimum 6-month retention
- Article 14: Human oversight capability — requires causal context capture, not just I/O logs
- Article 26: Deployer obligations — the enterprise bears compliance responsibility, not the LLM provider
- Article 49: Registration in EU database before deployment

Vendor-native logs (OpenAI, Anthropic consoles) do not satisfy Article 26's independence requirement. KYDE's out-of-band ledger is architecturally independent of the providers it logs.

**DORA (EU Regulation 2022/2554)**
In force since January 2025. Applies to financial entities. Article 30 requires ICT-related incident logs, up to two-year retention, independent of ICT third-party providers. KYDE's provider-independent ledger directly addresses this requirement.

**GDPR Article 22 / 35**
Automated decision-making requirements and DPIA obligations apply to AI agent deployments in HR, credit, insurance, and healthcare. Causal context capture supports Article 22 explainability requirements.

**UK DRCF (CMA, FCA, ICO, Ofcom)**
Joint foresight paper on agentic AI: organizational accountability is unchanged regardless of agent autonomy. "My agent did it" is not a defense. KYDE provides the audit infrastructure to demonstrate organizational control.

**NIST AI RMF**
US framework converging on identical requirements: traceable identity, causal context capture, tamper-evident records in a governance layer independent of the agents it governs.

## Target verticals (EU AI Act Annex III)

- HR Technology / Recruiting (employment decisions)
- Fintech / BNPL / Banking (credit scoring, risk assessment)
- Insurance (risk classification, claims, pricing)
- Healthcare administration (essential services)
- Critical infrastructure (energy, transport, water)
- Education technology (assessment, admission)

## Key differentiator vs. adjacent solutions

- **vs. AI security tools (Zenity, Lakera, Prompt Security)**: Those are semantic firewalls — they inspect inputs/outputs for adversarial content. KYDE is governance infrastructure — it enforces behavioral policy, provides agent identity, and produces compliance-grade audit trails. Analogous to: antivirus vs. corporate law.
- **vs. observability tools (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize)**: Those require framework-specific instrumentation and produce developer debug output. KYDE is framework-agnostic, out-of-band, and produces regulator-ready audit records with enforcement capability.
- **vs. platform-native governance (Microsoft Copilot Studio, AWS Bedrock Guardrails)**: Those govern within a single vendor's stack. KYDE governs the chain across all providers and platforms — the gap every hyperscaler leaves open because they cannot govern their competitors' infrastructure.
